## T40a i18n — `src/i18n`

- [x] I18nProvider → `i18n::I18n`, a gpui global: the shown locale and one catalog per locale
- [x] Trans / LocalizedText → `I18n::text`, a message with its `{name}` arguments filled
- [x] LocaleNumber / LocaleDate → `Locale::number` and `Locale::date`, CLDR's separators, right-to-left sign and short dates
- [x] RTL layout — proven: `Direction::row` mirrors a stack and `Direction::align` sets its text's side; a right-to-left line stays one `Ellipsis`, since gpui wraps glyphs in drawn order; Ely's other components stay left to right

## T40b a11y — `src/i18n`

- [ ] LiveRegion / Announcer — prove: gpui has no live setter, but `a11y_synthetic_children` hands over the element's own AccessKit node, which takes `set_live`; on macOS AccessKit then posts an announcement of the node's value when it appears and each time the value changes. A box with an id, a `role` and its words in `aria_value` must show each new value in the macOS tree. Neither that tree nor `Window::debug_a11y_tree_json` shows the live flag, and no process here is trusted to observe VoiceOver take the announcement
- [x] SkipLink → `i18n::SkipLink`: a Tab stop in flow that shows only while focused, raised over the page, and hands focus to its target
- [ ] AccessibleIcon — prove: an svg makes no node, so an `Icon` takes its name from a box around it with an id, `role(Role::Image)` and an `aria_label`; that box must reach the macOS tree with its name
- [ ] AriaLabel helper — prove: gpui's own `aria_label`, on an element with an id and a `role`; plain strings make no node, so a control's name goes on its box. A labeled button must reach the macOS tree with its name
- [x] KeyboardNavigationHelper → `interaction::RovingFocus`
- [ ] ScreenReaderOnly → VisuallyHidden (prove)
- [x] ColorBlindSafe Palette → `Theme::set_color_blind_safe`: chart hues fitted to stay apart under Machado's simulated protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia, each 3:1 on its page

## T41a Maps · View — `src/maps`

- [x] MapView — host tiles → `maps::MapView`: the host's tile for each zoom, column and row, the nearest cut scaled past its zooms; a drag, the wheel or the arrows pan, Command-wheel, + and - or its buttons zoom
- [x] MapMarker → `maps::MapMarker`, a pin keyed by its place's name, a Tab stop and pressable while in view when the map hears it; a focused pin keeps focus as it leaves the view
- [x] MapPopup → `maps::MapPopup`, over or under its point toward the larger half, held inside the map, its body scrolling past the room; it takes focus when it shows and hands it back when it goes
- [x] LocationPicker → `maps::LocationPicker`, the place under a center crosshair
- [x] CoordinateDisplay → `maps::CoordinateDisplay`, degrees or degrees, minutes and seconds, copyable

## T41b Maps · Layers

- [x] MapCluster → `MapView::cluster_markers`: pins gathered by squares of the world, so a pan keeps each group; a cluster's press shows its members whole
- [x] RouteLine → `maps::RouteLine`, a layer that crosses the date line the short way
- [x] GeoJSON Layer → `maps::read_geojson` reads RFC 7946 to features; `maps::GeoJsonLayer` washes areas with their holes open, strokes lines, dots points
- [x] GeoHeatmap (from T34) → `maps::GeoHeatmap`, weighted places as heat scaled to the densest spot in view

## T41c Maps · World

- [x] ChoroplethMap → `maps::ChoroplethMap` on a `ChoroplethLayer`: areas washed by value on one hue's scale, keyed by id or a property, with a legend; an area without a value reads as no data, a value without an area is logged once
- [x] WorldMap (from T34) → `maps::WorldMap`, Natural Earth's 110m countries bundled and washed by ISO 3166 alpha-2 code; a key that is no code fails

## T42f Misc · Web

- [x] IframeEmbed / EmbedCard → `misc::IframeEmbed`, a page in a frame of its own under its address, with Open in browser; EmbedCard is `chat::LinkPreviewCard`

- [x] ShareSheet → `buttons::ShareButton`

## T42g Misc · Export and import

- [x] ExportDialog — PDF, PNG, CSV, JSON → `misc::ExportDialog`: the owner's formats as cards, and Export hands the chosen one over for the owner to write; each way out answers once
- [x] ImportDialog — field mapping → `misc::ImportDialog`: a Select of the columns for each field, matched by name to start, over a preview of the first rows; Import asks for each required field's column
- [x] CSVImporter → `misc::CsvImporter`: CSV read as RFC 4180 (`misc::read_csv`), its first row naming the columns unless the box says otherwise, mapped through the ImportDialog into records; text that does not read says why
